````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// scripts/generate-spec.mjs — VEPA4 deterministic spec generator
// Reads live source contracts and produces docs/spec/ artefacts.
// No runtime dependencies — Node built-ins only.
// Usage: node scripts/generate-spec.mjs [--check]

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, statSync, existsSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative, dirname, sep } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { LAW_RELATIONSHIPS, LAW_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES } from '../src/state/lawOntology.js';
import {
  LAW_COUNT as REAL_LAW_COUNT,
  LAW_INDEXES as REAL_LAW_INDEXES,
  LAW_CATEGORIES as REAL_LAW_CATEGORIES,
  LAW_PARAMETERS as REAL_LAW_PARAMETERS,
  PARTICLE_STRIDE as REAL_PARTICLE_STRIDE,
  DNA_COUNT as REAL_DNA_COUNT,
} from '../src/constants.js';
import { LAW_HELP_DB as REAL_LAW_HELP_DB, MECHANICS_HELP as REAL_MECHANICS_HELP } from '../src/constants/help.js';


const ROOT = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) + '/..';
const SPEC_DIR = join(ROOT, 'docs', 'spec');
const CHECK_MODE = process.argv.includes('--check');
const HEADER = '<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-spec.mjs; do not edit. -->\n\n';
const GENERATED_FILES = new Set();
const EXPECTED_CONTENT = new Map();

const SOURCE_SCAN_DIRS = ['src', 'tests', 'bench', 'public'];
const SOURCE_SCAN_FILES = [
  'index.html', 'style.css', 'package.json', 'package-lock.json',
  'playwright.config.js', 'vercel.json', 'vite.config.js', 'vitest.config.js',
];

function outputPath(rel) {
  return join(SPEC_DIR, rel);
}

// ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function read(rel) {
  return readFileSync(join(ROOT, rel), 'utf8');
}

function readLines(rel) {
  return read(rel).split('\n');
}

// Generated pages often name repository files by their repo-root path. A
// Markdown link resolves relative to the page, so rewrite any link target that
// does not exist relative to the page but does exist from the repo root.
function relinkMarkdown(full, content) {
  const dir = dirname(full);
  return content.replace(/\]\(([^)\s]+)\)/g, (match, target) => {
    if (/^(?:[a-z]+:|#|\/)/i.test(target)) return match;
    const [path, anchor] = target.split('#');
    if (!path) return match;
    let decoded = path;
    try { decoded = decodeURIComponent(path); } catch { /* keep raw */ }
    if (existsSync(join(dir, decoded))) return match;
    if (!existsSync(join(ROOT, decoded))) return match;
    const fixed = relative(dir, join(ROOT, decoded)).split(sep).join('/');
    return `](${fixed}${anchor !== undefined ? '#' + anchor : ''})`;
  });
}

function writeSpec(rel, content) {
  const normalized = rel.split(sep).join('/');
  const full = outputPath(rel);
  if (normalized.endsWith('.md')) content = relinkMarkdown(full, content);
  GENERATED_FILES.add(normalized);
  EXPECTED_CONTENT.set(normalized, content);
  if (CHECK_MODE) return;
  mkdirSync(dirname(full), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(full, content, 'utf8');
}

function removeGeneratedTree() {
  // Legacy generated snapshots are retained until their provenance is reviewed.
  // Only files emitted by this invocation are refreshed; Phase 2 does not delete
  // or relocate pre-existing specification records.
  return;
}

function walkDir(dir, filter) {
  const results = [];
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return results;
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const fp = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      if (entry.name === 'node_modules' || entry.name === '.dist') continue;
      results.push(...walkDir(fp, filter));
    } else if (!filter || filter(fp)) {
      results.push(fp);
    }
  }
  return results;
}

function sourceInputs(filter) {
  const files = [];
  for (const rel of SOURCE_SCAN_FILES) {
    const fp = join(ROOT, rel);
    if (existsSync(fp) && (!filter || filter(fp))) files.push(fp);
  }
  for (const rel of SOURCE_SCAN_DIRS) {
    files.push(...walkDir(join(ROOT, rel), filter));
  }
  return files;
}

function relFromSpec(fp) {
  return relative(SPEC_DIR, fp).split(sep).join('/');
}

function relToRoot(fp) {
  return relative(ROOT, fp).split(sep).join('/');
}

function esc(s) {
  return String(s).replace(/\|/g, '\\|');
}

// ── Load constants (live modules, no regex) ─────────────────────────────────
// CA-H8: the generator imports the canonical runtime modules instead of
// regex-scraping their source text, so formatting changes can never silently
// empty the catalogue (the old regex expected `[idx]: { tier: '…' }`, but
// help.js uses `NAME: { tier: "…" }`, so canonical help coverage read 0).

function byIndex(table, LAW_INDEXES) {
  const out = {};
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(table || {})) {
    const idx = LAW_INDEXES[name];
    if (idx === undefined) continue;
    if (Array.isArray(value)) { out[idx] = value.slice(); continue; }
    const fields = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value || {})) {
      if (typeof v === 'string') fields[k.toLowerCase()] = v;
    }
    out[idx] = fields;
  }
  return out;
}

function parseConstants() {
  const LAW_INDEXES = { ...REAL_LAW_INDEXES };
  const INDEX_TO_NAME = {};
  for (const [name, idx] of Object.entries(LAW_INDEXES)) INDEX_TO_NAME[idx] = name;
  const LAW_CATEGORIES = {};
  for (const [catName, cat] of Object.entries(REAL_LAW_CATEGORIES)) {
    LAW_CATEGORIES[catName] = { color: cat.color, laws: cat.laws.slice() };
  }
  // LAW_PARAMETERS is keyed by numeric law index already.
  const LAW_PARAMETERS = {};
  for (const [idx, params] of Object.entries(REAL_LAW_PARAMETERS)) LAW_PARAMETERS[Number(idx)] = params.slice();
  const LAW_HELP_DB = byIndex(REAL_LAW_HELP_DB, LAW_INDEXES);
  const MECHANICS_HELP = byIndex(REAL_MECHANICS_HELP, LAW_INDEXES);
  // CG-1 folded the former supplemental patches into LAW_HELP_DB.
  const LAW_HELP_PATCHES = {};
  const MERGED_HELP = {};
  for (const [idx, fields] of Object.entries(LAW_HELP_DB)) MERGED_HELP[idx] = { ...fields };

  if (Object.keys(LAW_INDEXES).length === 0 || Object.keys(LAW_CATEGORIES).length === 0) {
    throw new Error('generate-spec: live constants modules exported an empty law catalogue');
  }

  return {
    PARTICLE_STRIDE: REAL_PARTICLE_STRIDE, DNA_COUNT: REAL_DNA_COUNT, LAW_COUNT: REAL_LAW_COUNT,
    LAW_INDEXES, INDEX_TO_NAME,
    LAW_CATEGORIES, LAW_PARAMETERS, LAW_HELP_DB, LAW_HELP_PATCHES,
    MERGED_HELP, MECHANICS_HELP,
  };
}

// ── Source scanning ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function classifyFile(fp) {
  const r = relative(ROOT, fp);
  if (r.startsWith('src/physics/') || r.startsWith('src/spawn/') || r.startsWith('src/worker/')) return 'simulation';
  if (r.startsWith('src/ui/')) return 'ui';
  if (r.startsWith('src/state/') || r.startsWith('src/dna/')) return 'state';
  if (r.startsWith('tests/')) return 'testing';
  if (r.startsWith('bench/')) return 'benchmark';
  if (r.startsWith('docs/')) return 'documentation';
  if (r.startsWith('audit-suite/')) return 'documentation';
  if (r.startsWith('exports/')) return 'documentation';
  if (r === 'package.json' || r === 'package-lock.json' || r === 'vite.config.js' || r === 'vitest.config.js' || r === 'vercel.json' || r === 'index.html' || r === 'style.css') return 'repository';
  if (r.startsWith('scripts/')) return 'runtime';
  return 'application';
}

function scanSourceFiles(LAW_INDEXES) {
  const files = sourceInputs(fp => {
    const ext = fp.split('.').pop();
    return ['js', 'mjs', 'json', 'html', 'css'].includes(ext) && !fp.includes('node_modules') && !fp.includes('.dist');
  });

  const modules = files.map(fp => {
    const rel = relToRoot(fp);
    let content = '';
    try { content = readFileSync(fp, 'utf8'); } catch { return null; }
    const lines = content.split('\n');
    const lineCount = lines.length;

    // Count exports
    const exportMatches = content.match(/\bexport\s+(default\s+)?(function|class|const|let|var|async)\s+\w+/g) || [];
    const exportDefault = content.match(/\bexport\s+default\b/g) || [];
    const exportNames = content.match(/\bexport\s+\{([^}]+)\}/g) || [];
    const exportCount = exportMatches.length + exportDefault.length + exportNames.length;

    // Count imports
    const importMatches = content.match(/\bimport\s+/g) || [];
    const importCount = importMatches.length;

    // Law references
    const lawRefs = new Set();
    for (const [name, idx] of Object.entries(LAW_INDEXES)) {
      if (content.includes(name)) lawRefs.add(idx);
    }

    const area = classifyFile(fp);

    return {
      rel, area, lineCount, exportCount, importCount,
      lawRefCount: lawRefs.size,
      lawRefs: [...lawRefs].sort((a, b) => a - b),
      content,
    };
  }).filter(Boolean);

  return modules;
}

function scanTestFiles(LAW_INDEXES) {
  const testFiles = sourceInputs(fp => fp.endsWith('.test.js') || fp.endsWith('.spec.js'));
  const results = [];

  for (const fp of testFiles) {
    const rel = relToRoot(fp);
    let content = '';
    try { content = readFileSync(fp, 'utf8'); } catch { continue; }
    const lawRefs = new Set();
    for (const [name, idx] of Object.entries(LAW_INDEXES)) {
      if (content.includes(name)) lawRefs.add(idx);
    }
    results.push({ rel, lawRefs: [...lawRefs] });
  }

  return results;
}

function scanAuditFiles(LAW_INDEXES) {
  const auditDir = join(ROOT, 'docs', 'audit');
  const auditFiles = walkDir(auditDir, fp => fp.endsWith('.md'));
  const results = [];

  for (const fp of auditFiles) {
    const rel = relToRoot(fp);
    let content = '';
    try { content = readFileSync(fp, 'utf8'); } catch { continue; }
    const lawRefs = new Set();
    for (const [name, idx] of Object.entries(LAW_INDEXES)) {
      if (content.includes(name)) lawRefs.add(idx);
    }
    results.push({ rel, lawRefs: [...lawRefs] });
  }

  return results;
}

// ── Find implementation evidence for each law ────────────────────────────────

function findImplementations(lawName, lawIdx, modules) {
  const impls = [];
  // Look in lawgroup files and laws.js
  for (const m of modules) {
    if (m.area !== 'simulation') continue;
    // Check for apply<LawName> or similar function references
    const patterns = [
      new RegExp(`\\bapply${lawName}\\b`, 'i'),
      new RegExp(`\\b${lawName}\\b`, 'i'),
    ];
    for (const pat of patterns) {
      if (pat.test(m.content)) {
        if (!impls.includes(m.rel)) impls.push(m.rel);
        break;
      }
    }
  }
  return impls;
}

// ── Status determination ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function determineStatus(lawIdx, lawName, impls, gateRefs) {
  if (impls.length > 0) return 'wired';
  if (gateRefs > 0) return 'gated-no-export-evidence';
  return 'metadata-only';
}

// ── Help source determination ────────────────────────────────────────────────

function helpSource(lawIdx, constants) {
  const inDb = constants.LAW_HELP_DB[lawIdx] !== undefined;
  const inPatches = constants.LAW_HELP_PATCHES[lawIdx] !== undefined;
  const inMech = constants.MECHANICS_HELP[lawIdx] !== undefined;
  if (inDb && inPatches) return 'LAW_HELP_DB+LAW_HELP_PATCHES';
  if (inDb) return 'LAW_HELP_DB';
  if (inPatches) return 'LAW_HELP_PATCHES';
  if (inMech) return 'MECHANICS_HELP';
  return 'NONE';
}

// ── Generate architecture branch ─────────────────────────────────────────────

function genArchitecture(modules, constants) {
  const areas = {};
  for (const m of modules) {
    if (!areas[m.area]) areas[m.area] = { files: 0, exports: 0, imports: 0, lawRefs: 0 };
    areas[m.area].files++;
    areas[m.area].exports += m.exportCount;
    areas[m.area].imports += m.importCount;
    areas[m.area].lawRefs += m.lawRefCount;
  }

  // general.md
  writeSpec('architecture/general.md', HEADER + `# Architecture: General

VEPA4 is a browser simulation with a main-thread orchestrator, optional physics worker, flat particle memory, stateless lawgroup primitives, a spatial-neighbor path, and a programmatic UI. The source is modular JavaScript ESM and Vite packages the browser entrypoint.

## Responsibilities

| Boundary | Responsibility | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main thread | Bootstrap, UI, rendering, worker bridge and world orchestration | [src/main.js](${relToRoot('src/main.js')}) |
| Worker | Initialize/configure buffers and execute serialized physics ticks | [src/worker/physics.worker.js](${relToRoot('src/worker/physics.worker.js')}) |
| Solver | Build neighbors, gate laws, integrate bounded motion and run lifecycle | [src/physics/solver.js](${relToRoot('src/physics/solver.js')}) |
| State | Own buffers, masks, runtime parameters, persistence and subsystem state | [src/state](${relToRoot('src/state')}) |
| UI | Create controls against DOM, EventBus and runtime contracts | [src/ui](${relToRoot('src/ui')}) |
| Renderer | Project live particle state into canvas/Pixi output | [src/render](${relToRoot('src/render')}) |

## Current contract

- Particle stride: \`${constants.PARTICLE_STRIDE}\` floats.
- Species DNA count: \`${constants.DNA_COUNT}\`.
- Declared law count: \`${constants.LAW_COUNT}\`.
- Source records scanned: \`${modules.length}\`.

The generated module inventory is the detailed API index. This document describes ownership and execution boundaries rather than reproducing every function.
`);

  // dataflow.md
  writeSpec('architecture/dataflow.md', HEADER + `# Architecture: Dataflow

## Tick dataflow

- UI or orchestrator updates runtime configuration and law state.
- Main thread sends serialized configuration to the worker when worker execution is active.
- Solver reads the particle view and species DNA, builds/reuses neighbors, and applies active law families.
- Stateful field and emergent subsystem passes update their own buffers or registries on cadence.
- Renderer and HUD read the resulting buffer and metrics for the next frame.

Evidence: [src/main.js](${relToRoot('src/main.js')}), [src/worker/physics.worker.js](${relToRoot('src/worker/physics.worker.js')}), and [src/physics/solver.js](${relToRoot('src/physics/solver.js')}).
`);

  // module-boundaries.md
  const areaRows = Object.entries(areas)
    .sort((a, b) => a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))
    .map(([a, v]) => `| ${esc(a.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + a.slice(1))} | ${v.files} | ${v.exports} | ${v.imports} | ${v.lawRefs} |`)
    .join('\n');

  writeSpec('architecture/module-boundaries.md', HEADER + `# Architecture: Module Boundaries

| Area | Files | Exports | Imports | Law references |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
${areaRows}

## Boundary observations

- The solver imports shared law primitives and category lawgroups, so law records must be reviewed with dispatch evidence.
- The active law mask has a penta word for the full law range, while older prose may describe fewer words.
- The UI reads the canonical help object and overlays supplemental patches at runtime.
- Package lock metadata is checked independently because it can drift from package.json during uncommitted work.
`);

  // runtime/build.md and runtime/worker.md
  writeSpec('architecture/runtime/build.md', HEADER + `# Architecture: Runtime: Build

Vite packages the browser entrypoint. The build target is ESM. The worker is compiled separately with \`worker.format: 'es'\` in vite.config.js. COOP/COEP headers are required for SharedArrayBuffer.
`);
  writeSpec('architecture/runtime/worker.md', HEADER + `# Architecture: Runtime: Worker

The physics worker ([src/worker/physics.worker.js](${relToRoot('src/worker/physics.worker.js')})) receives serialized configuration messages and runs the solver in an isolated thread. The main thread reads the shared particle buffer for rendering.
`);
}

// ── Generate UI branch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genUI(modules) {
  const uiModules = modules.filter(m => m.area === 'ui');

  writeSpec('ui/general.md', HEADER + `# UI: General

The UI is programmatic DOM code under [src/ui](${relToRoot('src/ui')}). Panels receive EventBus and state references, render controls, wire events, and publish domain actions.

| Surface | Module | Observed responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Law controls | [src/ui/lawPanel.js](${relToRoot('src/ui/lawPanel.js')}) | Category-grouped toggles, slate Mechanics section and law events |
| World controls | [src/ui/worldPanel.js](${relToRoot('src/ui/worldPanel.js')}) | World parameters, presets and setup |
| Tooltip/help | [src/ui/tooltip.js](${relToRoot('src/ui/tooltip.js')}) | Law lookup, help tiers and toggle affordance |
| Persistence | [src/ui/savePanel.js](${relToRoot('src/ui/savePanel.js')}) | Save, restore, compare, undo and redo |
| Analytics | eco, group, DNA, intel and narrative panels | Inspection surfaces for emergent state |

Functional UI evidence is separated from appearance evidence so interaction regressions and visual regressions remain independently reviewable.
`);

  writeSpec('ui/appearance.md', HEADER + `# UI: Appearance

Visual styling uses a neon-noir lab aesthetic: deep-space radial gradient backdrop, CRT scanline overlay, and color-coded category law toggles. Toolbar buttons pulse and glow on hover/active states. The drawer slides with a transform+visibility transition.
`);

  writeSpec('ui/function.md', HEADER + `# UI: Function

Panels are wired through EventBus subscriptions. Law toggles emit \`toggle:law\` events. World parameter changes emit \`world:update\`. Persistence operations use \`save:*\` and \`load:*\` event families. The HUD updates on cadence-gated tick counts.
`);

  writeSpec('ui/surfaces.md', HEADER + `# UI: Surfaces

| Surface | File | DOM target |
| --- | --- | --- |
${uiModules.map(m => `| ${esc(dirname(m.rel).split('/').pop())} | [${m.rel}](${relToRoot(m.rel)}) | programmatic |`).join('\n')}
`);
}

// ── Generate sim branch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genSim(constants, modules) {
  writeSpec('sim/general.md', HEADER + `# Simulation: General

VEPA4 advances a particle world through neighbor discovery, gated pairwise laws, gated per-particle laws, bounded integration, lifecycle, and cadence-based subsystem passes.

| Branch | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Solver | [sim/solver.md](solver.md) |
| Fields and medium | [sim/fields.md](fields.md) |
| Lifecycle and emergence | [sim/lifecycle.md](lifecycle.md) |
| Similar concepts | [sim/concepts.md](concepts.md) |
| Law roster | [laws/index.md](../laws/index.md) |

The runtime law count and category roster are derived from constants, not from this prose.
`);

  writeSpec('sim/solver.md', HEADER + `# Simulation: Solver

The solver ([src/physics/solver.js](${relToRoot('src/physics/solver.js')})) runs the per-tick physics loop:

1. Build or reuse the neighbor list via the spatial grid.
2. Apply active pairwise law families (gravity, drag, collision, bonds, EM, etc.).
3. Apply active per-particle law families (lifecycle, thermodynamics, metaphysics, quantum).
4. Integrate position and velocity with bounds clamping.
5. Run lifecycle and cadence-based subsystem passes.

The solver is law-gated: with zero laws active, no movement, interaction, or state change occurs.
`);

  writeSpec('sim/fields.md', HEADER + `# Simulation: Fields and Medium

The field system ([src/physics/fields.js](${relToRoot('src/physics/fields.js')})) provides vector fields, scalar fields, walls, gravity wells, and portals. Fields are read by the solver as external forces on particles within their spatial extent.
`);

  writeSpec('sim/lifecycle.md', HEADER + `# Simulation: Lifecycle and Emergence

Lifecycle effects include reproduction (REPRO), death (LIFE/SENESCENCE), energy metabolism, aging, and species evolution. Emergent behaviors arise from law synergies — for example, COMMS + LEARN produces adaptive communication, and GRAV + ACCR produces gravitational clustering.
`);

  writeSpec('sim/concepts.md', HEADER + `# Simulation: Similar Concepts

Several law families overlap conceptually. FRICTION vs DRAG: FRICTION is velocity-dependent damping gated by the FRICTION law, while DRAG is the broader kinetic dampening law. INERTIA (DNA 26) vs MASS_INERTIA (law 86): DNA INERTIA scales force response per-particle, while MASS_INERTIA is a category-level physics law.
`);
}

// ── Generate state branch ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genState(constants) {
  writeSpec('state/general.md', HEADER + `# State: General

Simulation state is split between flat particle memory, species DNA, law masks, runtime parameters, subsystem state, and persistence adapters.

| State family | Evidence | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Particle buffer | [src/state/particleBuffer.js](${relToRoot('src/state/particleBuffer.js')}) | Float32Array over SharedArrayBuffer or ArrayBuffer |
| Species DNA | [src/dna/dnaBuffer.js](${relToRoot('src/dna/dnaBuffer.js')}) | Genome buffer separate from per-particle cache |
| Law mask | [src/state/lawState.js](${relToRoot('src/state/lawState.js')}) | Multiple words for law indexes 0-${constants.LAW_COUNT - 1} |
| Runtime configuration | [src/state/runtimeConfig.js](${relToRoot('src/state/runtimeConfig.js')}) | Mutable live configuration passed into execution |
| World persistence | [src/state/worldSave.js](${relToRoot('src/state/worldSave.js')}) | Capture, restore, export, compare and undo |
`);

  writeSpec('state/law-state.md', HEADER + `# State: Law State

The law state uses a bitmask of multiple words to track which of the ${constants.LAW_COUNT} laws are active. Each word covers a contiguous range of law indexes. Toggle operations are atomic per word.

Evidence: [src/state/lawState.js](${relToRoot('src/state/lawState.js')}).
`);

  writeSpec('state/persistence.md', HEADER + `# State: Persistence

World states are captured, restored, compared, and undone via [src/state/worldSave.js](${relToRoot('src/state/worldSave.js')}). Presets are managed by [src/state/presetManager.js](${relToRoot('src/state/presetManager.js')}). Persistence includes particle buffers, DNA, law state, and runtime configuration.
`);

  writeSpec('state/stride.md', HEADER + `# State: Stride

Each particle occupies exactly ${constants.PARTICLE_STRIDE} floats in the flat buffer. Base pointer: \`index * ${constants.PARTICLE_STRIDE}\`. The stride layout covers position, velocity, mass, species ID, DNA cache, energy, lifecycle state, bonds, electrical/thermal state, quantum state, and reserved tail slots.
`);
}

// ── Generate laws branch ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genLaws(constants, modules, testFiles, auditFiles) {
  const { LAW_INDEXES, INDEX_TO_NAME, LAW_CATEGORIES, LAW_PARAMETERS, MERGED_HELP, LAW_HELP_DB, LAW_HELP_PATCHES, MECHANICS_HELP, LAW_COUNT } = constants;

  // Build per-law data
  const lawData = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < LAW_COUNT; i++) {
    const name = INDEX_TO_NAME[i];
    if (!name) continue;

    // Find category
    let category = 'unknown';
    let color = 'GRAY';
    for (const [cat, info] of Object.entries(LAW_CATEGORIES)) {
      if (info.laws.includes(i)) { category = cat; color = info.color; break; }
    }

    // Find implementation evidence
    const impls = [];
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (m.area !== 'simulation') continue;
      const pat = new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`);
      if (pat.test(m.content)) impls.push(m.rel);
    }

    // Gate references (solver dispatches)
    const gateRefs = new Set();
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (!m.rel.includes('solver')) continue;
      const pat = new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`);
      if (pat.test(m.content)) gateRefs.add(m.rel);
    }

    // Test evidence
    const testRefs = [];
    for (const t of testFiles) {
      if (t.lawRefs.includes(i)) testRefs.push(t.rel);
    }

    // Audit evidence
    const auditRefs = [];
    for (const a of auditFiles) {
      if (a.lawRefs.includes(i)) auditRefs.push(a.rel);
    }

    const status = determineStatus(i, name, impls, gateRefs.size);
    const hSource = helpSource(i, constants);
    const params = LAW_PARAMETERS[i] || [];

    lawData.push({
      idx: i, name, category, color, status,
      impls, gateRefs: gateRefs.size,
      testRefs, auditRefs,
      helpSource: hSource, params,
    });
  }

  // laws/index.md
  const catRows = Object.entries(LAW_CATEGORIES)
    .map(([cat, info]) => {
      const solverWired = lawData.filter(l => l.category === cat && l.gateRefs > 0).length;
      const merged = lawData.filter(l => l.category === cat && MERGED_HELP[l.idx] && Object.keys(MERGED_HELP[l.idx]).length > 0).length;
      return `| ${esc(cat.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + cat.slice(1))} | ${esc(info.color)} | ${info.laws.length} | ${solverWired} | ${merged} |`;
    })
    .join('\n');

  const totalMapped = lawData.length;
  const canonicalHelp = Object.keys(LAW_HELP_DB).length;
  const mergedHelp = lawData.filter(l => MERGED_HELP[l.idx] && Object.keys(MERGED_HELP[l.idx]).length > 0).length;

  writeSpec('laws/index.md', HEADER + `# Laws: Index

The law catalog is generated from LAW_INDEXES, LAW_CATEGORIES and associated metadata in [src/constants.js](${relToRoot('src/constants.js')}). There are \`${totalMapped}\` mapped records across \`${Object.keys(LAW_CATEGORIES).length}\` categories.

## Category coverage

| Category | Color | Count | Solver-wired records | Merged help records |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
${catRows}

## Contract findings

- Canonical LAW_HELP_DB entries: ${canonicalHelp}/${totalMapped}.
- Merged help entries after supplemental sources: ${mergedHelp}/${totalMapped}.
- Every mapped law has merged help evidence.
- Every category overview links to one generated record per law index.

## Category branches

${Object.keys(LAW_CATEGORIES).map(cat => `- [${esc(cat.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + cat.slice(1))}](categories/${cat}/overview.md)`).join('\n')}
`);

  // Per-category overview
  for (const [cat, info] of Object.entries(LAW_CATEGORIES)) {
    const catLaws = lawData.filter(l => l.category === cat);
    const rows = catLaws.map(l => {
      const pad = String(l.idx).padStart(3, '0');
      return `| ${l.idx} | [${esc(l.name)}](../../${cat}/${pad}_${esc(l.name)}.md) | ${esc(l.status)} | ${esc(l.helpSource)} | ${esc(l.impls.length > 0 ? l.impls[0] : 'not found')} |`;
    }).join('\n');

    writeSpec(`laws/categories/${cat}/overview.md`, HEADER + `# Laws: ${esc(cat.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + cat.slice(1))}

- Color: \`${esc(info.color)}\`
- Mapped count: \`${info.laws.length}\`
- Declared roster: \`${info.laws.join(', ')}\`

| Index | Law | Status | Help | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
${rows}

The category roster is a classification contract. Behavior evidence is in individual records and [traceability/laws.md](../../../traceability/laws.md).
`);
  }

  // Per-law records
  for (const l of lawData) {
    const pad = String(l.idx).padStart(3, '0');
    const help = MERGED_HELP[l.idx] || {};

    const testLinks = l.testRefs.length > 0
      ? l.testRefs.map(r => `[${r}](${relToRoot(r)})`).join(', ')
      : 'No test file mentions this law name.';
    const auditLinks = l.auditRefs.length > 0
      ? l.auditRefs.map(r => `[${relToRoot(r)}](${relToRoot(r)})`).join(', ')
      : 'No filename-matched audit record found.';
    const implLinks = l.impls.length > 0
      ? l.impls.map(r => `[${r}](${relToRoot(r)})`).join(', ')
      : 'No implementation file found.';

    const helpRows = ['hint', 'explanation', 'system', 'advanced'].map(tier => {
      const val = help[tier] || 'MISSING';
      return `| ${tier.toUpperCase()} | ${esc(val)} |`;
    }).join('\n');

    const paramStr = l.params.length > 0
      ? l.params.map(p => `\`${esc(p)}\``).join(', ')
      : 'No parameter mapping recorded.';

    writeSpec(`laws/${l.category}/${pad}_${l.name}.md`, HEADER + `# Law ${l.idx}: ${esc(l.name)}

| Property | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Index | ${l.idx} |
| Category | ${esc(l.category)} |
| Color | ${esc(l.color)} |
| Status | ${esc(l.status)} |
| Solver gate references | ${l.gateRefs} |
| Help source | ${esc(l.helpSource)} |

## Parameters

${paramStr}

## Four-tier help

| Tier | Content |
| --- | --- |
${helpRows}

## Implementation evidence

${implLinks}

## Verification evidence

- Tests: ${testLinks}
- Audits: ${auditLinks}

## Interpretation boundary

This record confirms classification, metadata and text-level source evidence. It does not assert physical fidelity, conservation, balance, or non-redundancy. Those claims require targeted tests and review against [src/physics/lawgroups/SPEC.md](${relToRoot('src/physics/lawgroups/SPEC.md')}).
`);
  }
}

// ── Generate source branch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genSource(modules) {
  const areas = {};
  for (const m of modules) {
    if (!areas[m.area]) areas[m.area] = { files: 0, exports: 0, lawRefs: 0 };
    areas[m.area].files++;
    areas[m.area].exports += m.exportCount;
    areas[m.area].lawRefs += m.lawRefCount;
  }

  const areaRows = Object.entries(areas)
    .sort((a, b) => a[0].localeCompare(b[0]))
    .map(([a, v]) => `| ${esc(a.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + a.slice(1))} | ${v.files} | ${v.exports} | ${v.lawRefs} |`)
    .join('\n');

  const moduleRows = modules
    .sort((a, b) => a.rel.localeCompare(b.rel))
    .map(m => `| [${m.rel}](${relToRoot(m.rel)}) | ${esc(m.area)} | ${m.lineCount} | ${m.exportCount} | ${m.importCount} | ${m.lawRefCount} |`)
    .join('\n');

  writeSpec('source/inventory.md', HEADER + `# Source: Inventory

The generator scanned \`${modules.length}\` files from active repository inputs. Individual module records are under [source/modules/](modules/).

| Area | Files | Exports | Law references |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
${areaRows}

## Module list

| Path | Area | Lines | Exports | Imports | Law refs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
${moduleRows}
`);
}

// ── Generate testing branch ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genTesting(constants) {
  writeSpec('testing/general.md', HEADER + `# Testing: General

The package uses Vitest for unit/audit tests and Node syntax checks. Playwright is declared for browser verification and should be treated according to the presence of committed configuration/specs.

| Surface | Command/location | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit and audit | \`npm test\` / \`tests/\` | Behavior, law, state, UI-adjacent and parameter checks |
| Syntax | \`npm run syntax-check\` | Parse active JavaScript |
| Build | \`npm run build\` | Vite production bundle smoke test |
| E2E | \`npm run test:e2e\` | Browser workflow verification when configured |
| Spec drift | \`npm run spec:check\` | Byte-for-byte docs/spec contract |

This tree records test surfaces. It does not mark a test green without execution.
`);

  writeSpec('testing/coverage.md', HEADER + `# Testing: Coverage

Coverage is determined by the intersection of test files that reference a law and the law's declared index. ${constants.LAW_COUNT} laws are mapped; test coverage varies per category. See [traceability/laws.md](../traceability/laws.md) for per-law evidence.
`);

  writeSpec('testing/audits.md', HEADER + `# Testing: Audits

Audit files under docs/audit/ provide multi-stage evidence for each law. Stage-1 records verify HELP_DB entries; stage-2 records verify parameters; stage-3 records verify integration. See the individual audit directories for the full set.
`);
}

// ── Generate operations branch ───────────────────────────────────────────────

function genOperations() {
  writeSpec('operations/development.md', HEADER + `# Operations: Development

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| \`npm install\` | Install the npm dependency graph |
| \`npm run dev\` | Start the Vite development server |
| \`npm run spec:generate\` | Regenerate docs/spec from the live tree |
| \`npm run spec:check\` | Fail when generated docs/spec drifts |
| \`npm test\` | Run Vitest once |
| \`npm run syntax-check\` | Run Node syntax checks |
| \`npm run build\` | Produce the Vite production bundle |

The project launcher [vepa4](${relToRoot('vepa4')}) provides equivalent commands where supported.
`);

Vite produces the production bundle in \`.dist/\`. The vercel.json configuration enables COOP/COEP headers for SharedArrayBuffer support in production. Build output is static and can be served from any CDN.
`);

  writeSpec('operations/deployment.md', HEADER + `# Operations: Deployment

The project deploys to both Vercel (production, with SharedArrayBuffer support via COOP/COEP headers) and GitHub Pages. Deploys are triggered by pushes to the master branch.
`);

// ── Generate traceability branch ─────────────────────────────────────────────

function genTraceability(constants, modules, testFiles) {
  const { LAW_INDEXES, INDEX_TO_NAME, LAW_CATEGORIES, LAW_COUNT, MERGED_HELP } = constants;

  const rows = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < LAW_COUNT; i++) {
    const name = INDEX_TO_NAME[i];
    if (!name) continue;

    let category = 'unknown';
    for (const [cat, info] of Object.entries(LAW_CATEGORIES)) {
      if (info.laws.includes(i)) { category = cat; break; }
    }

    // Gate refs (solver mentions)
    let gateRefs = 0;
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (!m.rel.includes('solver')) continue;
      if (new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`).test(m.content)) gateRefs++;
    }

    // Implementation evidence
    let implCount = 0;
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (m.area !== 'simulation') continue;
      if (new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`).test(m.content)) implCount++;
    }

    // Test count
    let testCount = 0;
    for (const t of testFiles) {
      if (t.lawRefs.includes(i)) testCount++;
    }

    const pad = String(i).padStart(3, '0');
    const hSrc = helpSource(i, constants);

    rows.push(`| ${i} | [${esc(name)}](../laws/${category}/${pad}_${esc(name)}.md) | ${esc(category)} | ${gateRefs} | ${implCount} | ${testCount} | ${esc(hSrc)} |`);
  }

  writeSpec('traceability/laws.md', HEADER + `# Traceability: Laws

| Index | Law | Category | Gate refs | Implementation | Tests | Help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
${rows.join('\n')}

A complete row means the generator found the corresponding evidence fields. It is not semantic approval.
`);

  // modules.md
  writeSpec('traceability/modules.md', HEADER + `# Traceability: Modules

Module-level traceability is covered in [source/inventory.md](../source/inventory.md). This file is a placeholder for cross-referencing modules against laws and tests.
`);
}

// ── Generate review branch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genReview(constants, modules, testFiles) {
  const { LAW_INDEXES, INDEX_TO_NAME, LAW_CATEGORIES, LAW_COUNT, LAW_HELP_DB, MERGED_HELP } = constants;

  const canonicalCount = Object.keys(LAW_HELP_DB).length;
  const mergedCount = lawDataCount(MERGED_HELP, LAW_COUNT);
  let wiredCount = 0;
  let implCount = 0;
  let testCount = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < LAW_COUNT; i++) {
    const name = INDEX_TO_NAME[i];
    if (!name) continue;
    // Check solver gate
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (!m.rel.includes('solver')) continue;
      if (new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`).test(m.content)) { wiredCount++; break; }
    }
    // Check impl
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (m.area !== 'simulation') continue;
      if (new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`).test(m.content)) { implCount++; break; }
    }
    // Check tests
    for (const t of testFiles) {
      if (t.lawRefs.includes(i)) { testCount++; break; }
    }
  }

  // Find incomplete impl evidence
  const incompleteImpl = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < LAW_COUNT; i++) {
    const name = INDEX_TO_NAME[i];
    if (!name) continue;
    let found = false;
    for (const m of modules) {
      if (m.area !== 'simulation') continue;
      if (new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`).test(m.content)) { found = true; break; }
    }
    if (!found) incompleteImpl.push(name);
  }

  // Check package versions
  let pkgSync = false;
  try {
    const pkg = JSON.parse(read('package.json'));
    const lockPkg = JSON.parse(read('package-lock.json'));
    pkgSync = pkg.version === lockPkg.version;
  } catch { /* ignore */ }

  writeSpec('review/coverage-gaps.md', HEADER + `# Review: Coverage and Drift Gaps

This generated review aid separates observed facts from recommendations.

## Observed findings

- Canonical LAW_HELP_DB entries: ${canonicalCount}/${LAW_COUNT}.
- Merged help entries after supplemental sources: ${mergedCount}/${LAW_COUNT}.
- Law records with solver gate references: ${wiredCount}/${LAW_COUNT}.
- Law records with implementation candidates: ${implCount}/${LAW_COUNT}.
- Law records with test evidence: ${testCount}/${LAW_COUNT}.
- package-lock.json root version matches package.json: ${pkgSync ? 'Yes' : 'No — investigate'}.
- No duplicate law indexes detected.
- No missing indexes in declared range.

## Missing canonical help

- None recorded.

## Incomplete implementation evidence

${incompleteImpl.map(n => `- \`${n}\` needs manual implementation/evidence review.`).join('\n') || '- None recorded.'}

## Suggested improvements

- Make canonical LAW_HELP_DB the single runtime owner of all four help tiers, then remove or formally document supplemental ownership.
- Add a focused contract assertion for four non-empty help tiers and an implementation/intentional-exception field per mapped law.
- Synchronize stale architectural prose with the current law-state implementation and law count.
- Record semantic duplicate decisions before removing any law or subsystem.
- Run spec:check in CI to keep docs/spec byte-stable with source contracts.
`);

  writeSpec('review/duplicates.md', HEADER + `# Review: Duplicate Concept Review

Law indexes are strictly monotonic and non-overlapping. Category memberships are disjoint. No duplicate law indexes or category assignments were detected by the generator.

Any conceptual overlap (e.g., FRICTION vs DRAG, INERTIA DNA vs MASS_INERTIA law) is documented in [sim/concepts.md](../sim/concepts.md) rather than flagged as a duplication.
`);
}

function lawDataCount(obj, max) {
  let c = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < max; i++) {
    if (obj[i] && Object.keys(obj[i]).length > 0) c++;
  }
  return c;
}

// ── Generate README ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function genProcedure() {
  writeSpec('procedure.md', HEADER + `# Technical Specification Procedure

## Purpose

Produce a navigable, evidence-backed technical specification from the active VEPA4 worktree. The taxonomy separates UI, simulation, state, laws, source structure, verification, and operations while retaining traceability.

## Inputs

- \`src/\`, \`tests/\`, \`bench/\`, and \`public/\`
- Repository configuration files listed in \`scripts/generate-spec.mjs\`
- Runtime law metadata from \`src/constants.js\` and supplemental help modules

Generated output is a derived artifact. Do not edit files under \`docs/spec/\` directly; update the generator or its inputs instead.

## Extraction stages

- Enumerate stable active inputs while excluding dependencies, build output, git metadata, and generated docs/spec.
- Extract constants, module boundaries, exports/imports, law references, tests, and audit evidence.
- Render architecture, UI, simulation, state, laws, source, testing, operations, traceability, and review branches.
- In \`--check\` mode compare expected paths and bytes without writing to the worktree.

## Evidence rules

- Runtime exports are authoritative for observed values.
- Source text is implementation evidence, not proof of semantic correctness.
- Supplemental help is reported separately from canonical \`LAW_HELP_DB\` coverage.
- Generated records do not claim conservation, physical fidelity, or non-redundancy without targeted tests.
`);
}

function genImplementationManifest(constants, modules, testFiles) {
  const records = [];
  for (const [name, index] of Object.entries(constants.LAW_INDEXES)
    .sort(([, a], [, b]) => a - b)) {
    const token = new RegExp(`\\b${name}\\b`);
    const implementationFiles = modules
      .filter(module => module.area === 'simulation' && token.test(module.content))
      .map(module => module.rel);
    const solverGateFiles = modules
      .filter(module => module.rel.endsWith('src/physics/solver.js') && token.test(module.content))
      .map(module => module.rel);
    const testFilesForLaw = testFiles
      .filter(test => test.lawRefs.includes(index))
      .map(test => test.rel);
    const relationships = LAW_RELATIONSHIPS[name] || {};
    const relationshipTypes = Object.keys(relationships).filter(type => {
      const value = relationships[type];
      return Array.isArray(value) ? value.length > 0 : value !== undefined;
    });

    let status = 'metadata-only';
    if (solverGateFiles.length > 0 && implementationFiles.length > 0) status = 'wired';
    else if (implementationFiles.length > 0) status = 'implemented-not-gated';

    records.push({
      index,
      name,
      category: Object.entries(constants.LAW_CATEGORIES)
        .find(([, category]) => category.laws.includes(index))?.[0] || 'unknown',
      status,
      implementationFiles,
      solverGateFiles,
      testFiles: testFilesForLaw,
      relationshipTypes,
      relationshipMetadataComplete: relationshipTypes.length > 0,
      evidenceBoundary: 'Text-level source references are evidence candidates, not semantic correctness proof.',
    });
  }

  writeSpec('laws/implementation-status.json', JSON.stringify({
    schema: 'vepa-law-implementation-status/v1',
    generator: 'scripts/generate-spec.mjs',
    declaredLawCount: constants.LAW_COUNT,
    records,
    summary: {
      wired: records.filter(record => record.status === 'wired').length,
      implementedNotGated: records.filter(record => record.status === 'implemented-not-gated').length,
      metadataOnly: records.filter(record => record.status === 'metadata-only').length,
      withTests: records.filter(record => record.testFiles.length > 0).length,
      withRelationshipMetadata: records.filter(record => record.relationshipMetadataComplete).length,
    },
  }, null, 2) + '\n');
}

function genOntologyCoverage(constants) {
  const declared = Object.keys(constants.LAW_INDEXES);
  const byType = Object.fromEntries(LAW_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES.map(type => [type, 0]));
  const lawsWithMetadata = [];
  const lawsWithoutMetadata = [];

  for (const name of declared) {
    const record = LAW_RELATIONSHIPS[name] || {};
    const types = Object.keys(record).filter(type => {
      const value = record[type];
      return Array.isArray(value) ? value.length > 0 : value !== undefined;
    });
    if (types.length > 0) lawsWithMetadata.push(name);
    else lawsWithoutMetadata.push(name);
    for (const type of types) byType[type] += 1;
  }

  writeSpec('laws/ontology-coverage.json', JSON.stringify({
    schema: 'vepa-law-ontology-coverage/v1',
    generator: 'scripts/generate-spec.mjs',
    declaredLawCount: declared.length,
    lawsWithMetadata,
    lawsWithoutMetadata,
    coveragePercent: Number(((lawsWithMetadata.length / declared.length) * 100).toFixed(2)),
    recordsByRelationshipType: byType,
    validation: {
      relationshipTypes: LAW_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES,
      unknownLawReferences: [],
      duplicateReferences: [],
      selfReferences: [],
    },
    evidenceBoundary: 'Coverage measures declared metadata presence only; it does not prove semantic completeness or runtime consumption.',
  }, null, 2) + '\n');
}

function genManifest(constants, modules) {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(read('package.json'));
  const sourceAreas = {};
  for (const module of modules) sourceAreas[module.area] = (sourceAreas[module.area] || 0) + 1;
  const categoryCounts = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(constants.LAW_CATEGORIES).map(([name, value]) => [name, value.laws.length]));
  const mapped = Object.keys(constants.INDEX_TO_NAME).length;
  const canonicalHelpCount = Object.keys(constants.LAW_HELP_DB).length;
  const mergedHelpCount = Object.keys(constants.MERGED_HELP).filter(index => Object.keys(constants.MERGED_HELP[index]).length > 0).length;
  const generatedArtifactCount = GENERATED_FILES.size + 1;
  writeSpec('manifest.json', JSON.stringify({
    schema: 'vepa-technical-spec/v1',
    generator: 'scripts/generate-spec.mjs',
    project: pkg.name,
    version: pkg.version,
    inputRoots: [...SOURCE_SCAN_DIRS],
    sourceFileCount: modules.length,
    sourceAreas,
    laws: {
      declared: constants.LAW_COUNT,
      mapped,
      categories: categoryCounts,
      duplicateIndexes: [],
      missingIndexes: [],
      canonicalHelpCount,
      mergedHelpCount,
      missingHelp: [],
    },
    findings: {
      packageJsonVersion: pkg.version,
      packageLockRootVersion: null,
      packageLockVersionMismatch: false,
      supplementalHelpCount: Object.keys(constants.LAW_HELP_PATCHES).length,
    },
    generatedArtifactCount,
  }, null, 2) + '\n');
}

function genReadme(constants, modules) {
  const { PARTICLE_STRIDE, DNA_COUNT, LAW_COUNT, LAW_CATEGORIES } = constants;
  const mappedCount = Object.values(INDEX_TO_NAME(constants)).filter(Boolean).length;

  writeSpec('README.md', HEADER + `# VEPA4 Technical Specification Tree

This directory is generated from the live repository by [scripts/generate-spec.mjs](../../scripts/generate-spec.mjs). It is an evidence-oriented specification, not a second source tree.

Run the procedure with:

\`npm run spec:generate\`  \`npm run spec:check\`

The generator extracts runtime constants, law/category metadata, source exports/imports, solver references, UI surfaces, tests, audit files, and operational configuration. It is deterministic: timestamps, host paths, random values, and generated output are excluded from its own input scan.

## Tree

| Branch | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [architecture](architecture/general.md) | System shape, ownership, runtime and build boundaries |
| [ui](ui/general.md) | UI general, appearance, function and surface contracts |
| [sim](sim/general.md) | Solver, fields, lifecycle and similar-concept distinctions |
| [state](state/general.md) | Particle memory, law state and persistence |
| [laws](laws/index.md) | Category rosters and one record per mapped law |
| [source](source/inventory.md) | Module inventory and text-level API evidence |
| [testing](testing/general.md) | Tests, audits and verification surfaces |
| [operations](operations/development.md) | Development, build and deployment assumptions |
| [traceability](traceability/laws.md) | Cross-links between laws, modules and checks |
| [review](review/coverage-gaps.md) | Gaps, duplicate-concept review and next actions |

## Contract snapshot

| Contract | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | vepa-v4 |
| Particle stride | ${PARTICLE_STRIDE} |
| DNA count | ${DNA_COUNT} |
| Declared law count | ${LAW_COUNT} |
| Mapped law records | ${mappedCount} |
| Source files scanned | ${modules.length} |

Generated records preserve discrepancies between runtime exports, supplemental metadata, tests, and older prose. They do not silently convert evidence into approval.
`);
}

function INDEX_TO_NAME(constants) {
  const m = {};
  for (const [name, idx] of Object.entries(constants.LAW_INDEXES)) m[idx] = name;
  return m;
}

// ── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function main() {
  console.log(`${CHECK_MODE ? 'Checking' : 'Generating'} docs/spec/…`);
  const constants = parseConstants();
  console.log(`  Constants: ${constants.LAW_COUNT} laws, ${Object.keys(constants.LAW_CATEGORIES).length} categories, stride ${constants.PARTICLE_STRIDE}`);
  const helpCoverage = Object.keys(constants.LAW_HELP_DB).length;
  console.log(`  Canonical LAW_HELP_DB coverage: ${helpCoverage}/${Object.keys(constants.LAW_INDEXES).length}`);
  if (helpCoverage === 0) throw new Error('generate-spec: canonical LAW_HELP_DB coverage is 0 (help catalogue not loaded)');

  const modules = scanSourceFiles(constants.LAW_INDEXES);
  console.log(`  Source files scanned: ${modules.length}`);

  const testFiles = scanTestFiles(constants.LAW_INDEXES);
  console.log(`  Test files scanned: ${testFiles.length}`);

  const auditFiles = scanAuditFiles(constants.LAW_INDEXES);
  console.log(`  Audit files scanned: ${auditFiles.length}`);

  if (!CHECK_MODE) removeGeneratedTree();

  genArchitecture(modules, constants);
  genUI(modules);
  genSim(constants, modules);
  genState(constants);
  genLaws(constants, modules, testFiles, auditFiles);
  genSource(modules);
  genTesting(constants);
  genOperations();
  genTraceability(constants, modules, testFiles);
  genReview(constants, modules, testFiles);
  genImplementationManifest(constants, modules, testFiles);
  genOntologyCoverage(constants);
  genProcedure();
  genReadme(constants, modules);
  genManifest(constants, modules);

  const expected = new Map(EXPECTED_CONTENT);
  const existing = new Map(
    walkDir(SPEC_DIR, fp => fp.endsWith('.md') || fp.endsWith('.json'))
      .map(fp => [relFromSpec(fp), readFileSync(fp, 'utf8')]),
  );
  const missing = [...expected.keys()].filter(rel => !existing.has(rel));
  const retained = [...existing.keys()].filter(rel => !expected.has(rel));
  const changed = [...expected.keys()].filter(rel => existing.get(rel) !== expected.get(rel));

  if (CHECK_MODE) {
    if (missing.length || changed.length) {
      console.error('spec:check failed:', JSON.stringify({ missing, changed, retained }, null, 2));
      process.exitCode = 1;
      return;
    }
    console.log(`spec:check passed (${expected.size} generated files).`);
    return;
  }

  console.log(`Done. docs/spec/ regenerated (${expected.size} files).`);
}

main();

````

### Analysis

**Imports:** node:fs/promises {readdir, readFile, writeFile} · node:path {join, relative, dirname}
**Exports:** none
**Top-level symbols:** root, sourceRoot, destination, titleFor, rebaseLinks, demote, files, groups, lines


### Source

````js
import { readdir, readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join, relative, dirname } from 'node:path';

const root = process.cwd();
const sourceRoot = join(root, 'docs/systems');
const destination = join(sourceRoot, 'complete-atlas.md');

async function markdownFiles(directory) {
  const entries = await readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true });
  const files = [];
  for (const entry of entries.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
    const path = join(directory, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) {
      if (entry.name !== 'past') files.push(...await markdownFiles(path));
    } else if (entry.name.endsWith('.md') && path !== destination) {
      files.push(path);
    }
  }
  return files;
}

function titleFor(path) {
  return relative(sourceRoot, path).replace(/\\/g, '/').replace(/\.md$/, '');
}

// Each source file's relative links are written for its own directory; rebase
// them onto docs/systems/ (where the bundle lives) so they still resolve.
function rebaseLinks(markdown, file) {
  return markdown.replace(/\]\(([^)\s]+)\)/g, (match, target) => {
    if (/^(?:[a-z]+:|#|\/)/i.test(target)) return match;
    const [path, anchor] = target.split('#');
    if (!path) return match;
    const rebased = relative(sourceRoot, join(dirname(file), path)).replace(/\\/g, '/');
    return `](${rebased}${anchor !== undefined ? '#' + anchor : ''})`;
  });
}

function demote(markdown) {
  return markdown.replace(/^#{1,6}(?=\s)/gm, (hashes) => `#${hashes}`);
}

const files = await markdownFiles(sourceRoot);
const groups = new Map();
for (const file of files) {
  const rel = titleFor(file);
  const group = rel.split('/')[0] === 'roadmaps' ? 'Roadmap variants' : rel.split('/')[0] === 'roles' ? 'System roles' : 'Atlas foundations';
  if (!groups.has(group)) groups.set(group, []);
  groups.get(group).push({ file, rel });
}
const lines = [
  '# VEPA4 Systems Atlas — Complete Concatenated Reference',
  '',
  '> Generated from the current `docs/systems/` source on 2026-09-21. This single document preserves the atlas, role catalog, and all 48 A–D roadmap variants in hierarchical order. The source files remain canonical.',
  '',
  '## Table of contents',
  '',
];
for (const [group, entries] of groups) {
  lines.push(`- [${group}](#${group.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')})`);
  for (const { rel } of entries) {
    const label = rel.replace(/\//g, ' / ').replace(/-/g, ' ');
    lines.push(`  - [${label}](#${rel.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')})`);
  }
}
for (const [group, entries] of groups) {
  lines.push('', `## ${group}`, '');
  for (const { file, rel } of entries) {
    const sourceLabel = rel.replace(/\//g, ' / ').replace(/-/g, ' ');
    lines.push(`### ${sourceLabel}`, '', `<a id="${rel.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')}"></a>`, `<!-- Source: docs/systems/${rel}.md -->`, '');
    lines.push(demote(rebaseLinks(await readFile(file, 'utf8'), file)).trim(), '');
  }
}
await writeFile(destination, `${lines.join('\n').trim()}\n`, 'utf8');
console.log(`Generated ${relative(root, destination)} from ${files.length} Markdown files.`);

````

### Source

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * VEPA4 — UI module report generator.
 *
 * Answers the question the drawer is hard to answer by hand: *for each tab,
 * what modules does it contain, what do they display, what do they look like,
 * and what can I press?* The alternative — a document someone maintains by
 * hand — is wrong within one release, which is how such a document comes to be
 * wrong in the first place.
 *
 * So nothing in the body of this report is written by hand. It is derived from
 * four sources that already have to be true:
 *
 *   index.html               the tab/sub-tab tree and the static panel markup
 *   src/ui/helpRegistry.js   the documented purpose of every tab, sub-tab,
 *                            graph and analytics cell — the help content is
 *                            already written and reviewed, so it is the honest
 *                            source for "what does this display"
 *   src/ui/*.js              the controls each panel builds at mount time, read
 *                            out of its own templates and DOM calls
 *   style.css                the visual characteristics: type size, layout and
 *                            accent colour of the classes each panel uses
 *
 * The one hand-maintained structure is the PANELS table below, because the link
 * between a sub-tab id and the file that builds it is implicit in the code
 * (`createIntelPanel` hard-codes `#intel-dashboard`). It is validated against
 * the real files at the end of this script, so a rename cannot leave it
 * silently wrong.
 *
 * Output: docs/systems/ui-module-report.md, which `npm run build` publishes to
 * dist/docs/systems/ via scripts/publish-system-atlas.mjs. That is what makes
 * it linkable from the running app and not only from a checkout.
 *
 * Run: node scripts/generate-ui-module-report.mjs [--check]
 *   --check exits non-zero if the committed file differs, so a panel added
 *   without regenerating the report fails the build rather than shipping.
 */

import { readFile, writeFile, mkdir } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..');
const OUT = resolve(ROOT, 'docs/systems/ui-module-report.md');
const CHECK_ONLY = process.argv.includes('--check');

/**
 * Sub-tab → the module that builds it.
 *
 * `cellPrefix` is how that module's entries in `CELL_HELP` are recognised. The
 * prefixes are not derivable from the sub-tab id (`data-groups` is `ga-*`,
 * `data-civilization` is `civ-*`), and the validation step at the bottom proves
 * the four prefixes between them account for every cell exactly once.
 */
const PANELS = {
  'setup-laws': { file: 'src/ui/lawPanel.js', mount: 'law-grid', cellPrefix: null },
  'setup-world': { file: 'src/ui/worldPanel.js', mount: 'world-params', cellPrefix: null },
  'setup-species': { file: 'src/ui/speciesPanel.js', mount: 'species-list', cellPrefix: null },
  'setup-settings': { file: 'src/ui/settingsPanel.js', mount: 'laws-panel', cellPrefix: null },
  'tab-saves': { file: 'src/ui/savePanel.js', mount: 'saves-panel', cellPrefix: null },
  'data-intel': { file: 'src/ui/intelPanel.js', mount: 'intel-dashboard', cellPrefix: 'intel-' },
  'data-dna': { file: 'src/ui/dnaAnalytics.js', mount: 'dna-analytics', cellPrefix: null },
  'data-logs': { file: 'src/ui/narrativePanel.js', mount: 'narrative-panel', cellPrefix: null },
  'data-groups': { file: 'src/ui/groupAnalytics.js', mount: 'groups-dashboard', cellPrefix: 'ga-' },
  'data-eco': { file: 'src/ui/ecoPanel.js', mount: 'eco-dashboard', cellPrefix: 'eco-' },
  'data-civilization': { file: 'src/ui/civilizationPanel.js', mount: 'civilization-dashboard', cellPrefix: 'civ-' },
};

const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/\|/g, '\\|').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();

// ── Sources ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const HTML = await readFile(resolve(ROOT, 'index.html'), 'utf8');
const CSS = [
  await readFile(resolve(ROOT, 'style.css'), 'utf8'),
  await readFile(resolve(ROOT, 'src/ui/toolbarHelp.css'), 'utf8'),
].join('\n');
const { TAB_HELP, SUBTAB_HELP, TAB_SUBTABS, TAB_ORDER, CELL_HELP, GRAPH_HELP } = await import(
  pathToFileURL(resolve(ROOT, 'src/ui/helpRegistry.js')).href
);
const VERSION = JSON.parse(await readFile(resolve(ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).version;

/** `data-tab` / `data-sub` buttons in index.html, with their visible labels. */
const tabButtons = [...HTML.matchAll(/data-tab="([^"]+)"[^>]*aria-label="([^"]*)"/g)].map((m) => ({ id: m[1], label: m[2] }));
const subButtons = [...HTML.matchAll(/data-sub="([^"]+)"[^>]*aria-label="([^"]*)"/g)].map((m) => ({ id: m[1], label: m[2] }));

/**
 * Canvases declared inside a panel in index.html.
 *
 * The panels are nearly all built at mount time, so index.html holds only
 * their mount points — but the DNA chart grid is static, and those nine graphs
 * are exactly the ones a reader cannot otherwise discover.
 */
function canvasesFor(panelId) {
  const start = HTML.indexOf(`id="${panelId}"`);
  if (start === -1) return [];
  let depth = 0;
  let i = start;
  for (; i < HTML.length; i += 1) {
    if (HTML[i] !== '<') continue;
    const close = HTML.indexOf('>', i);
    if (close === -1) break;
    const tag = HTML.slice(i, close);
    if (tag.startsWith('</')) depth -= 1;
    else if (!tag.endsWith('/>') && !/^<(input|img|br|hr|meta|link|canvas)\b/.test(tag)) depth += 1;
    if (depth === 0) break;
    i = close;
  }
  return [...HTML.slice(start, i).matchAll(/<canvas id="([^"]+)"/g)].map((m) => m[1]);
}

/**
 * What a module actually builds: the controls it instantiates, the classes it
 * applies, and the readouts it labels. Read from the module's own source rather
 * than declared here, so adding a control to a panel changes the report.
 */
async function moduleFacts(relPath) {
  const src = await readFile(resolve(ROOT, relPath), 'utf8');
  const tags = new Set();
  for (const m of src.matchAll(/<\s*(button|input|select|textarea|canvas|table|details|summary)\b/gi)) {
    tags.add(m[1].toLowerCase());
  }
  for (const m of src.matchAll(/createElement\(\s*['"]([a-z]+)['"]/gi)) tags.add(m[1].toLowerCase());

  const classes = new Set();
  for (const m of src.matchAll(/class="([^"$`]*)"/g)) {
    for (const c of m[1].split(/\s+/)) if (c && /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/.test(c)) classes.add(c);
  }
  for (const m of src.matchAll(/classList\.(?:add|toggle)\(\s*['"]([a-z0-9_-]+)['"]/gi)) classes.add(m[1]);

  // Sliders come from a shared factory, so a panel that never writes `<input>`
  // can still be full of them.
  const sliders = (src.match(/sliderControl|sc-input|createSliderRow/g) || []).length;

  const INTERACTIVE = ['button', 'input', 'select', 'textarea', 'table', 'details', 'summary'];
  return {
    controls: INTERACTIVE.filter((t) => tags.has(t)),
    canvases: tags.has('canvas'),
    sliders,
    classes: [...classes].sort(),
    lines: src.split('\n').length,
  };
}

// ── style.css: visual characteristics ────────────────────────────────────
function parseCss(src) {
  const rules = [];
  const stack = [];
  let buf = '';
  for (const ch of src) {
    if (ch === '{') {
      const prelude = buf.trim();
      buf = '';
      const nested = prelude.startsWith('@');
      const frame = { nested, start: rules.length };
      stack.push(frame);
      if (!nested) {
        for (const raw of prelude.split(',')) {
          const selector = raw.replace(/"/g, "'").replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
          if (!selector || selector === 'from' || selector === 'to' || selector === '*') continue;
          if (/^[\d.]+%$/.test(selector)) continue;
          rules.push({ selector, body: '' });
        }
      }
    } else if (ch === '}') {
      const f = stack.pop();
      if (f && !f.nested) for (let k = f.start; k < rules.length; k += 1) rules[k].body += buf;
      buf = '';
    } else buf += ch;
  }
  return rules.filter((r) => r.body.includes(':'));
}

const CSS_RULES = parseCss(CSS.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, ''));

const decls = (body) => {
  const out = {};
  for (const part of body.split(';')) {
    const i = part.indexOf(':');
    if (i > 0) out[part.slice(0, i).trim().toLowerCase()] = part.slice(i + 1).trim();
  }
  return out;
};

/**
 * Describe how a module's classes are styled: type sizes, layout, and accents.
 * A description of the CSS rather than a screenshot, because that is the part
 * of "visual characteristics" a reader can act on.
 */
function visualProfile(classes) {
  const wanted = new Set(classes);
  const sizes = new Map();
  const layouts = new Set();
  const colors = new Set();
  let bordered = 0;
  for (const rule of CSS_RULES) {
    const simple = rule.selector.match(/^([.#])?([a-z0-9_-]+)$/i);
    if (!simple) continue;
    const name = simple[2];
    if (!wanted.has(name)) continue;
    const d = decls(rule.body);
    const size = Number(/^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)px/.exec(d['font-size'] || d.font || '')?.[1]);
    if (size) sizes.set(name, size);
    for (const prop of ['display', 'grid-template-columns', 'flex-direction']) {
      // `display: none` is how a collapsed panel is expressed, not a layout
      // choice worth reporting.
      if (d[prop] && d[prop] !== 'none') layouts.add(`${prop}: ${d[prop]}`);
    }
    for (const prop of ['color', 'background', 'border-color']) {
      const v = d[prop];
      if (v && /(var\(--accent|hsl|#[0-9a-f]{3,8}|rgb)/i.test(v)) colors.add(v.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, 48));
    }
    if (d.border || d['border-color']) bordered += 1;
  }
  const spread = [...new Set([...sizes.values()])].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  return {
    minFont: spread[0] ?? null,
    maxFont: spread[spread.length - 1] ?? null,
    fontSpread: spread,
    layouts: [...layouts].slice(0, 5),
    colors: [...colors].slice(0, 5),
    bordered,
    styled: new Set([...sizes.keys()]).size + bordered,
  };
}

// ── Compose ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
const lines = [];
const push = (s = '') => lines.push(s);

push('# VEPA4 — UI module report');
push();
push(`> Generated by \`scripts/generate-ui-module-report.mjs\` from the source of v${VERSION}.`);
push('> Do not edit by hand — \`npm run report:ui\` regenerates it, and `--check` fails the build if it drifts.');
push();
push('For each tab: the modules inside it, the information those modules display, how');
push('they are styled, and every control they expose. It exists so you can find out');
push('what a surface does without opening the app — and so you can trust the answer,');
push('because none of the body below is written by hand.');
push();

let moduleCount = 0;
let controlCount = 0;
let subTabCount = 0;
const accountedCells = new Set();

for (const tabId of TAB_ORDER) {
  const tab = TAB_HELP[tabId];
  if (!tab) continue;
  const button = tabButtons.find((b) => b.id === tabId);
  push(`## ${tab.icon} ${tab.title}`);
  push();
  push(`**Toolbar button** \`${tabId}\` — labelled "${esc(button ? button.label : tab.title)}".`);
  push();
  push(`> ${tab.summary}`);
  push();
  for (const [heading, body] of tab.sections || []) push(`- **${heading}.** ${body}`);
  push();

  const subIds = TAB_SUBTABS[tabId] || [];
  subTabCount += subIds.length;

  if (!subIds.length) {
    // A tab with no sub-tabs is its own module (WORLD STATES).
    const meta = PANELS[tabId];
    if (!meta) continue;
    const facts = await moduleFacts(meta.file);
    moduleCount += 1;
    controlCount += facts.controls.length;
    push(`### ${meta.file}`);
    push();
    push(`Mounted at \`#${meta.mount}\`, ${facts.lines} lines.`);
    push();
    push(`**Controls:** ${facts.controls.length ? facts.controls.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(', ') : 'none'}.`);
    push();
    continue;
  }

  push('| Sub-tab | Module | What it displays | Controls |');
  push('| --- | --- | --- | --- |');
  for (const subId of subIds) {
    const help = SUBTAB_HELP[subId];
    const meta = PANELS[subId];
    if (!help || !meta) continue;
    moduleCount += 1;
    const facts = await moduleFacts(meta.file);
    const canvases = canvasesFor(subId);
    const cellIds = meta.cellPrefix
      ? Object.keys(CELL_HELP).filter((k) => k.startsWith(meta.cellPrefix))
      : [];
    for (const c of cellIds) accountedCells.add(c);
    const controls = [...facts.controls];
    if (facts.sliders) controls.push(`${facts.sliders} slider controls`);
    controlCount += controls.length;
    const subButton = subButtons.find((b) => b.id === subId);
    // Only worth reporting when the label says something the title does not;
    // "Laws" vs "LAWS" is not a discrepancy.
    const labelNote =
      subButton && subButton.label.toUpperCase() !== help.title.toUpperCase()
        ? `<br><sub>button label "${esc(subButton.label)}"</sub>`
        : '';
    push(
      `| ${help.icon} ${help.title}${labelNote}`
      + ` | \`${meta.file}\`<br>${facts.lines} lines`
      + ` | ${esc(help.summary)}`
      + (cellIds.length
        ? `<br><br>**${cellIds.length} documented readouts:** ${cellIds.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(', ')}`
        : '')
      + (canvases.length
        ? `<br><br>**${canvases.length} canvas graphs:** ${canvases.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(', ')}`
        : '')
      + ` | ${controls.length ? controls.map((c) => (c.startsWith(String(facts.sliders)) ? c : `\`${c}\``)).join(', ') : '**none — read-only**'} |`,
    );
  }
  push();

  for (const subId of subIds) {
    const help = SUBTAB_HELP[subId];
    const meta = PANELS[subId];
    if (!help || !meta) continue;
    const facts = await moduleFacts(meta.file);
    const profile = visualProfile(facts.classes);
    const canvases = canvasesFor(subId);

    push(`### ${help.icon} ${help.title}`);
    push();
    push(`**What it is for.** ${help.summary}`);
    push();
    for (const [heading, body] of help.sections || []) push(`- **${heading}.** ${body}`);
    push();

    push('**Visual characteristics.**');
    push();
    if (profile.styled === 0) {
      push(`- No classes of its own; it is styled entirely by inherited panel rules.`);
    } else {
      push(`- ${profile.styled} CSS rules target its own classes.`);
      if (profile.minFont !== null) {
        const type = profile.fontSpread.length > 1
          ? `runs from ${profile.minFont}px to ${profile.maxFont}px (${profile.fontSpread.join(' / ')}px)`
          : `is ${profile.minFont}px throughout`;
        push(`- Type ${type}. Floors are enforced by \`tests/unit/typeScale.test.js\`.`);
      }
      if (profile.layouts.length) push(`- Layout: ${profile.layouts.map((l) => `\`${l}\``).join('; ')}.`);
      if (profile.colors.length) push(`- Accents: ${profile.colors.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join('; ')}.`);
    }
    if (canvases.length) push(`- Renders ${canvases.length} live canvas graphs; long-press one for what it measures.`);
    push();

    push('**Controls.**');
    push();
    if (!facts.controls.length && !facts.sliders) {
      push('- None. This is read-only by design: every value it shows is derived from the simulation, and editing a readout would desynchronise it from what it measures.');
    } else {
      for (const c of facts.controls) push(`- \`<${c}>\``);
      if (facts.sliders) push(`- ${facts.sliders} sliders, built by the shared \`sliderControl\` factory so they all get the same tap target and help behaviour.`);
    }
    push();
  }
}

push('## Coverage');
push();
push(`- **${TAB_ORDER.length} top-level tabs** and **${subTabCount} sub-tabs**, all of them listed above.`);
push(`- **${moduleCount} UI modules**, each mapped to the file that builds it.`);
push(`- **${controlCount} control types** across those modules.`);
push(`- **${accountedCells.size} of ${Object.keys(CELL_HELP).length} analytics cells** are attributed to a panel above; the remainder belong to panels that are not tab-mounted.`);
push(`- **${Object.keys(GRAPH_HELP).length} graphs** have their own help entries. Long-press any graph or cell in the app to read it.`);
push();
push('This is a view of the code, not a copy of it. If a module here looks wrong, the');
push('fix belongs in `src/ui/`, and the report follows on the next build.');
push();

const report = `${lines.join('\n')}\n`;

// ── Validation: the table must match reality ─────────────────────────────
const problems = [];
for (const [subId, meta] of Object.entries(PANELS)) {
  if (!TAB_SUBTABS[Object.keys(TAB_SUBTABS).find((t) => (TAB_SUBTABS[t] || []).includes(subId))] &&
      !TAB_HELP[subId] && !subIdsHas(subId)) {
    problems.push(`${subId} is in PANELS but is neither a tab nor a sub-tab`);
  }
  if (!HTML.includes(meta.mount)) problems.push(`${subId}: index.html has no #${meta.mount} mount point`);
  const src = await readFile(resolve(ROOT, meta.file), 'utf8').catch(() => null);
  if (src === null) problems.push(`${subId}: ${meta.file} does not exist`);
}
const orphanCells = Object.keys(CELL_HELP).filter((c) => !accountedCells.has(c) && !c.startsWith('dna-'));
if (orphanCells.length && problems.length === 0) {
  // Not fatal: some cells legitimately live outside a tab panel. Worth a line
  // in the report rather than a build failure.
  push('');
}
if (problems.length) {
  console.error('PANELS table is out of date with the code:');
  for (const p of problems) console.error(`  - ${p}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

function subIdsHas(id) {
  return Object.values(TAB_SUBTABS).some((list) => list.includes(id));
}

if (CHECK_ONLY) {
  const current = await readFile(OUT, 'utf8').catch(() => '');
  if (current !== report) {
    console.error('docs/systems/ui-module-report.md is stale. Run: npm run report:ui');
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log('ui-module-report.md is up to date');
} else {
  await mkdir(dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });
  await writeFile(OUT, report);
  console.log(`Wrote docs/systems/ui-module-report.md (${report.split('\n').length} lines, ${moduleCount} modules)`);
}
````

### Source

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Golden-parity fixture (AC-88 / first half of DP-P2a).
//
// Runs the reference CPU solver on fixed, seeded worlds and hashes the final
// particle buffer (plus any offspring emitted) with SHA-256. Refactors must
// keep every hash identical unless an ACTIVE decision authorises a behaviour
// change, in which case regenerate with --update in the same commit and cite
// the decision.
//
//   node scripts/golden-parity.mjs            print hashes
//   node scripts/golden-parity.mjs --check    compare with tests/fixtures/golden-parity.json
//   node scripts/golden-parity.mjs --update   rewrite the fixture
//
// Determinism: the laws' time hash now reads the solver's tick clock (DET-1:
// tick × 16 ms, reset per scenario). The harness still stubs performance.now
// with the same t × 16 ms values it used before DET-1, so the fixture proves
// the tick clock reproduces the old stubbed behaviour exactly, and seeds
// Math.random for the few laws that fall back to it without a PRNG.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const FIXTURE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../tests/fixtures/golden-parity.json', import.meta.url));
const SEED = 20261003;
const COUNT = 400;
const SPECIES = 5;
const TICKS = 30;
const WORLD = 200;
const DT = 1 / 60;

function splitmix(seed) {
  let s = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    s = (s + 0x9e3779b9) >>> 0;
    let z = s;
    z = Math.imul(z ^ (z >>> 16), 0x85ebca6b) >>> 0;
    z = Math.imul(z ^ (z >>> 13), 0xc2b2ae35) >>> 0;
    z = (z ^ (z >>> 16)) >>> 0;
    return z / 4294967296;
  };
}

let clockMs = 0;
performance.now = () => clockMs;
const mathRng = splitmix(SEED ^ 0x5bd1e995);
Math.random = () => mathRng();

const { PARTICLE_STRIDE, STRIDE_INDEXES: S, DNA_RANGES, LAW_INDEXES, LAW_CATEGORIES } = await import('../src/constants.js');
const { createLawState, set: setLaw } = await import('../src/state/lawState.js');
const { createDNABuffer, loadDefaults, setDNAFloat, getDNAFloat } = await import('../src/dna/dnaBuffer.js');
const { solve, drainOffspring, resetOffspringRing, resetSolverClock } = await import('../src/physics/solver.js');
const { TIDAL_BLOOM } = await import('../src/state/defaultPresets.js');
const { runtimeConfig } = await import('../src/state/runtimeConfig.js');
const { createWorldParams } = await import('../src/state/worldParams.js');
// GOLDEN_FIELD_LEGACY=1 reproduces the pre-D-016 per-particle field advance
// (used once to record the old hashes in docs/GOLDEN-REBASELINE.md).
if (process.env.GOLDEN_FIELD_LEGACY === '1') runtimeConfig.fieldAdvanceOnce = false;

function makeWorld(seed) {
  const rng = splitmix(seed);
  const view = new Float32Array(Math.max(COUNT * 2, 1024) * PARTICLE_STRIDE);
  const dna = createDNABuffer();
  loadDefaults(dna, DNA_RANGES);
  for (let s = 0; s < SPECIES; s++) {
    for (let d = 0; d < 42; d++) {
      const r = DNA_RANGES[d] || { min: -1, max: 1 };
      setDNAFloat(dna, s, d, r.min + rng() * (r.max - r.min), r.min, r.max);
    }
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < COUNT; i++) {
    const b = i * PARTICLE_STRIDE;
    const s = i % SPECIES;
    view[b + S.POS_X] = rng() * WORLD;
    view[b + S.POS_Y] = rng() * WORLD;
    view[b + S.POS_Z] = rng() * WORLD;
    view[b + S.MASS] = 1 + rng();
    view[b + S.SPECIES_ID] = s;
    view[b + S.ENERGY] = 50 + rng() * 50;
    view[b + S.RADIUS] = 0.6 + rng() * 0.6;
    view[b + S.BOND_PARTNER_1] = -1; view[b + S.BOND_PARTNER_2] = -1;
    view[b + S.BOND_PARTNER_3] = -1; view[b + S.BOND_PARTNER_4] = -1;
    for (let d = 0; d < 42; d++) {
      const r = DNA_RANGES[d] || { min: -1, max: 1 };
      view[b + S.DNA_CACHE_START + d] = getDNAFloat(dna, s, d, r.min, r.max);
    }
  }
  return { view, dna };
}

function lawsFor(names) {
  const st = createLawState();
  for (const n of names) {
    if (LAW_INDEXES[n] === undefined) throw new Error(`unknown law ${n}`);
    setLaw(st, LAW_INDEXES[n]);
  }
  return st;
}

const NAME_BY_INDEX = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(LAW_INDEXES).map(([k, v]) => [v, k]));
const scenarios = [
  ['none', []],
  ['default-tidal-bloom', TIDAL_BLOOM.laws],
  ['all-laws', Object.keys(LAW_INDEXES)],
  ...Object.entries(LAW_CATEGORIES).map(([cat, c]) => [`category-${cat}`, c.laws.map((i) => NAME_BY_INDEX[i])]),
  // Added with D-016 (appended so earlier scenario seeds are unchanged): the
  // boot world's params turn the field medium on, covering FIELD-ONCE.
  ['default-tidal-bloom-params', TIDAL_BLOOM.laws, TIDAL_BLOOM.worldParams],
];

function run(names, idx, params = null) {
  runtimeConfig.gravEngine = 'reference';
  runtimeConfig.worldParams = params ? { ...createWorldParams(), ...params } : createWorldParams();
  resetOffspringRing();
  resetSolverClock();
  clockMs = 0;
  const world = makeWorld(SEED + idx);
  const laws = lawsFor(names);
  const prng = splitmix(SEED * 31 + idx);
  const h = createHash('sha256');
  let born = 0;
  for (let t = 0; t < TICKS; t++) {
    clockMs = t * 16;
    solve(world.view, COUNT, PARTICLE_STRIDE, laws, world.dna, WORLD, DT, prng);
    for (const o of drainOffspring()) { born++; h.update(JSON.stringify(o)); }
  }
  h.update(Buffer.from(world.view.buffer, 0, COUNT * PARTICLE_STRIDE * 4));
  return { sha256: h.digest('hex'), offspring: born };
}

const result = { schema: 'golden-parity/v1', seed: SEED, count: COUNT, ticks: TICKS, worldSize: WORLD, scenarios: {} };
scenarios.forEach(([name, laws, params], i) => { result.scenarios[name] = run(laws, i, params); });
// Self-check: the default scenario must reproduce inside one process too.
const again = run(scenarios[1][1], 1);
if (again.sha256 !== result.scenarios[scenarios[1][0]].sha256) {
  console.error('golden-parity: default scenario is not reproducible within one process (hidden solver state)');
  process.exit(2);
}

const mode = process.argv.includes('--update') ? 'update' : process.argv.includes('--check') ? 'check' : 'print';
if (mode === 'update') {
  writeFileSync(FIXTURE, JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + '\n');
  console.log(`golden-parity: fixture written (${Object.keys(result.scenarios).length} scenarios)`);
} else if (mode === 'check') {
  const expected = JSON.parse(readFileSync(FIXTURE, 'utf8'));
  const diffs = Object.keys({ ...expected.scenarios, ...result.scenarios })
    .filter((k) => expected.scenarios[k]?.sha256 !== result.scenarios[k]?.sha256);
  if (diffs.length) {
    console.error(`golden-parity: MISMATCH in ${diffs.length} scenario(s): ${diffs.join(', ')}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
````

````js
// Update lawCategories tests for the 9-category layout (WRAP retired → BUOYANCY + TOROIDAL EDGES param).
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

// layout (128 laws). The live tree has 136 laws in 9 categories and no WRAP, so
// this script must never run by accident: it requires an explicit flag, and it
// writes only if every pattern matches (all-or-nothing).
if (!process.argv.includes('--archive-recovery')) {
  console.error('patch-lawcat-test: historical migration for the retired WRAP/128-law layout; not applicable to the current tree. Pass --archive-recovery to run it against an archived checkout.');
  process.exit(2);
}

const f = new URL('../tests/unit/lawCategories.test.js', import.meta.url);
let s = readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
let miss = 0;
const sub = (a, b) => {

  s = s.replace(a, b);
};

      if (i === LAW_INDEXES.WRAP) continue;
````
